newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium warns Zaire against eastern offensive.
newsitem.headline: Belgium warns Zaire against eastern offensive.

text.p: Belgium said on Tuesday Zaire's threat to launch a military offensive against rebels in the east of the country could damage prospects of a peaceful end to the wider human crisis gripping the Great Lakes region.

"Any military offensive cannot but damage prospects for such a (peaceful) solution and cause new suffering for a civilian population that has already been dangerously weakened," the foreign ministry said in a statement.

Belgium respected Zaire's territorial integrity, but believed a lasting solution to the region's crisis would only come about after Zaire held free elections and through dialogue within a planned Great Lakes Conference, the ministry said.

Zaire's Prime Minister Kengo Wa Dondo told the nation on Monday he had formally ordered the armed forces to launch a counter-offensive to recapture territory held by Tutsi-led rebels in the east of the country.
It was not immediately clear what impact Kengo's comments would have on the timing of the counter-thrust, which has been promised for over a month.
Witnesses have reported the regular arrival of Zairean troops and mercenaries in recent weeks in the eastern town of Kisangani.
Three Russian-built attack helicopters, bristling with missiles and 24 mm cannon, were seen circling over the town and outlying villages on Sunday and Monday.
